findings.title: process() method has multiple responsibilities
findings.description: The process() function handles 4 distinct concerns: claiming job, executing, posting result, updating status. This violates Single Responsibility Principle and makes testing difficult.
findings.suggestion: Extract into separate methods: claim(), execute(), postResult(), markComplete(). Each can be tested independently.
findings.currentCode: Lines 117-121: claim, Lines 124: execute, Lines 127-129: post, Lines 131-138: mark_final
findings.benefit: Easier to test error scenarios, easier to modify individual steps.

findings.title: Anonymous response envelope struct not named
findings.description: The response envelope struct (lines 106-108) is defined inline and not reusable. If the same structure is used elsewhere, it's redefined.
findings.suggestion: Define at package level: type JobsResponse struct { Data []Job `json:"data"` }
findings.benefit: Improves reusability and explicit API contract.

findings.title: Comments could be more descriptive
findings.description: Comments describe WHAT the code does, not WHY. For example, line 90 'calls GET /api/jobs...' just repeats the code.
examples: Line 105: // Coordinator returns a paginated envelope (good context!)
findings.improvement: Add comment explaining the retry logic for claiming: 'Claim job atomically to prevent duplicate processing by other agents'
findings.impact: Low - existing comments are mostly adequate.

findings.title: Repeated JSON marshaling pattern
findings.description: Both updateStatus() and postResult() create inline maps and marshal them to JSON. This pattern is repeated.
findings.suggestion: Consider a helper method or use json.RawMessage for cleaner code.
findings.impact: Very low - code is still clear.
